evals.prompt: I have a Rex agent named 'reviewer' already running in my tab. Ask it to summarize the open PRs and show me what it says back.
evals.expected_output: Runs agent.py check, resolves reviewer by exact label with agent.py get, then sends and waits in one `agent.py prompt reviewer "..." --timeout N` call rather than rex send plus a sleep or a hand-rolled capture loop. Maps blocked / stalled / timeout to distinct outcomes, reads the reply with `agent.py read <block> --turn <turn>` using the turn ID the prompt printed, and relays only the delta.
expectations: The prompt goes through `agent.py prompt` (one call that preflights, sends, and waits), not raw `rex send` followed by sleep or repeated captures.
The reply is read with `agent.py read ... --turn <id>` (the prompt's turn ID) and only the relevant delta is relayed.

The run ends with a final report: Result first (COMPLETE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED), then Evidence naming only checks that ran, Uncertainty listing UNKNOWN values and unchecked replies, and Decision naming the approval needed or 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: Spin up two Rex agents for this project named 'tests' and 'docs'. Use pi with thinking low for both. Put them beside my pane so I see root + both agents in one tab.
evals.expected_output: Runs agent.py check, resolves the launch profile once and relays its summary, then starts each worker with `launch_profile.py --start tests --kind pi --thinking low --cwd <project>` (and docs), which splits the rightmost column, equalizes all columns, and waits for an idle program status. Does not create new windows, does not pass the main agent's Claude model or effort to pi, and confirms with agent.py fleet before assigning work.
expectations: Each worker is started with `launch_profile.py --start <name> --kind pi --thinking low`, not with a hand-built `rex split -- pi ...` command.
Both workers land as columns in the root window (no `--new-window`, no `rex window new`), and the run reports equal column widths.
No Claude model ID or effort value is passed to the pi workers.
The launch-profile summary line is resolved as its own call and relayed before the first start.

The run ends with a final report: Result first (COMPLETE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED), then Evidence naming only checks that ran, Uncertainty listing UNKNOWN values and unchecked replies, and Decision naming the approval needed or 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: I'm done with all my Rex fleet agents for this project — shut them down.
evals.expected_output: Treats teardown as destructive: lists the worker blocks this run knows, asks for explicit confirmation, then closes only those worker blocks with `rex block close -s <session> <full block IDs>`, keeping the root block. Never closes the session or window unless asked, never stops the Rex server or kills Rex processes. If the user does not confirm, closes nothing and records the teardown as skipped.
expectations: The agent asks for confirmation before closing anything.
Only worker blocks are closed, by full block ID; the root block, the session, and the Rex server are left alone.

The run ends with a final report: Result first (COMPLETE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED), then Evidence naming only checks that ran, Uncertainty listing UNKNOWN values and unchecked replies, and Decision naming the approval needed or 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: Keep driving this Rex fleet through the whole refactor — I don't want the run to fall over when you fill up your own context.
evals.expected_output: Treats its own context as a gated resource: self-checks at the gate points (before a spawn wave, before a broadcast, after each relayed reply), continues below 50%, and at or above it (or on the UNKNOWN fallback: 20 relayed reads or 4 spawn waves) starts a successor with `launch_profile.py --start main-g2`, sends the handoff brief through agent.py prompt, reads the ack `HANDOFF ACCEPTED gen=2 fleet=<k>` (the successor then waits), sends `GO gen=2`, then goes read-only and focuses the successor with rex focus.
expectations: The context gate is checked at the named gate points, with a percentage or an explicit UNKNOWN fallback log line.
A HANDOFF starts the successor through `launch_profile.py --start main-g<N>` on the inherited profile and waits for the exact ack before going read-only.

The run ends with a final report: Result first (COMPLETE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED), then Evidence naming only checks that ran, Uncertainty listing UNKNOWN values and unchecked replies, and Decision naming the approval needed or 'No approval needed.'
